terminals.name: e2e-stack
terminals.command: export E2E_FAKE_HTTPS_PORT=${E2E_FAKE_HTTPS_PORT:-443} && make e2e-env-up && .cursor/trust-fake-google.sh && echo 'E2E stack is healthy' && cd e2e/playwright && docker compose logs -f --tail 0
terminals.description: Boots the stack from e2e/playwright/docker-compose.yml and then tails its logs: Mattermost at http://localhost:8085, Postgres on 5435, and a fake Google (e2e/playwright/fake-google/server.ts) standing in for Google's OAuth, Meet and Calendar APIs. Wait for 'E2E stack is healthy'. There is no real Google here and no Google credentials: never run anything against real Google. The server starts with no users: create the first account in the browser (it becomes the system admin; a fresh browser lands on /landing, so click 'View in Browser'), or run the Playwright suite once, which creates sysadmin / Sys@dmin-sample1. Build and install the plugin with `MM_SERVICESETTINGS_SITEURL=http://localhost:8085 MM_ADMIN_USERNAME=<admin> MM_ADMIN_PASSWORD=<password> make deploy` (run it again after every plugin change). Then in System Console > Plugins > Google Meet set Google OAuth Client ID fake-client-id.apps.googleusercontent.com and Google OAuth Client Secret fake-client-secret, click Regenerate next to Encryption Key, and Save. SiteURL must stay http://localhost:8085: the fake only accepts OAuth callbacks on localhost. accounts.google.com is mapped to the fake in /etc/hosts, so `/meet connect` opens the fake's sign-in page: choose Meet Owner (meet-owner@fake-google.test) or Meet Guest (meet-guest@fake-google.test), keep the scopes checked and click Continue; the popup closes itself. `/meet start` or the app bar button then creates a space in the fake; the meeting tab it opens goes to the real meet.google.com, which does not know that meeting code, as expected. Fake Google's control API (http://127.0.0.1:8100/__control/...): GET requests (every Google call the plugin made), GET violations (calls that break Google's API contract; should be empty), POST conferences {space: <meeting code>, startOffsetSeconds: -600, endOffsetSeconds: -60} and POST artifacts {conference: <record name>, kind: recording|transcript|smartNote} to simulate a finished meeting, then trigger the poller as an admin with POST http://localhost:8085/plugins/com.mattermost.google-meet/api/v1/admin/poll-now. See e2e/playwright/README.md. Server and plugin logs: `cd e2e/playwright && docker compose logs mattermost`. Automated tests: `make e2e` from the repo root, or `cd e2e/playwright && npx playwright test specs/<spec>.spec.ts`; they replace the plugin's settings, so configure it again afterwards. Reset all data with `make e2e-env-down && make e2e-env-up && .cursor/trust-fake-google.sh` (a reset generates a new CA, so the trust script must run again).
